title: Dune Buggy update: a forest rally stage, plus a promo Claude planned, shot and cut
author: laht1
selftext:
Another update on the off-road racer I’m building with Claude Code on threepp, my C++20/Vulkan 3D library with Python bindings.

New since last time is a 4.9 km gravel rally stage through a forest with about 93k scanned pines, spruces and birches. That makes 4 maps (Dune Sea, Butte Valley, Kettle Hill MX, Furuskog) and 3 cars (sandrail, beach buggy, trophy truck), and every map works by day and by night.

Claude also made the video and the race song. 

threepp: [github.com/markaren/threepp](http://github.com/markaren/threepp)

comments.author: dustandwater
comments.body:
This looks great overall, and is exactly the sort of thing that should be promoted in the debate around AI dev.

That said, there are a couple of things that stand out to me as AI identifiers. The main issue is the physics and the “weight” of the cars. For some reason, the cars just don’t feel grounded in the video. They seem to be moving around, and there happens to be a floor underneath them, but I’m barely convinced the two things are connected.

The cars need to feel more heavily affected by gravity. They need to hit the ground with more weight after a jump. I don’t know if this is early on, and you just haven’t got to that yet? But it will elevate the gameplay experience immensely.

replies.author: laht1
replies.body: Honestly, I didn't even plan to make a game at all and we'll see how far I'll take it. At the very least it's a nice test arena for my renderer.  Anyhow, the issues you are surfacing are partly because of two features: Landing assist and Post-landing damping.  Gravity is a real 9.81, but the assists levels the car in the air so it always lands flat on four wheels. On top of that, extra damping right after touchdown stops it bouncing back.

replies.author: dustandwater
replies.body:
Nice. The answer shows you actually know what you’re doing while you build. This is the sort of thing they refuse to believe over on the other, non-AI dev subs. 

I frequently insist that there are games or developments like this being made with Claude by developers like you, and then they ask, ‘Okay, show us just one example of something that’s actually good.’ 

This is exactly the sort of thing that people need to see to start believing, I think.

comments.body: Forest stage looks solid — that gravel run through the pines feels like a real rally vibe.

replies.body: You need a RTX5080 to run it at 60 FPS though :D Working on optimizing it.

replies.author: maisuwei
replies.body: A bit disappointing if it needs a 5080 for 60 — hope the next pass brings it down.
